The ATTEND study collects clinical records, radiology imaging, IHC, and WES-derived
genomic features (TMB, MSI, HRD, aneuploidy, and a per-variant MAF) on the **same
patients**. These reports link the modalities onto a shared patient ID, assemble a
per-patient master table, and analyse it.

**Each report answers one question on one cohort**, and says so in a four-line scope
contract at the top: the question, the cohort, what it reads, and what it deliberately
leaves to another report. The number states the stage — `1x` build, `2x` QC, `3x`
findings, `4x` external — and the gaps absorb future reports without renumbering.

[10_data_integration](10_data_integration.html) writes
`output/clean_data/attend_master_joined` (Parquet, or CSV without `arrow`), and every
later report reads that one file back through `code/attend_io.R`.

**[00 — Methods](00_methods.html)** carries every justification in the pipeline: why a
distance metric, why a correction, why a threshold. Operational recipes — how to run
GISTIC on the cluster, what the classification alternatives are — live in `runbooks/`.

### 1x — Build

- **[10 — Data integration](10_data_integration.html)** · all patients
  Translates three ID spaces onto one patient key, collapses each modality to one row per
  patient, recomputes the TMB definitions, and **writes `attend_master_joined`**.
- **[11 — Join audit](11_join_audit.html)** · all patients
  What the join cost: records that never reached a patient, coverage per dataset, the
  UpSet of which patients have which modalities, and value sanity on the joined table.

### 2x — QC and validation

- **[20 — FlowPath vs the pathologist](20_flowpath_concordance.html)** · all imaged
  Does the automated quantification agree with the pathologist's eye, on continuous
  measures and categorical calls.
- **[21 — Covariate distributions by MMR status](21_covariates_by_mmr.html)** · all patients
  ECDF and Kolmogorov–Smirnov per continuous covariate, plus the aneuploidy score itself
  contrasted between MMR-deficient and -proficient tumours.

### 3x — Findings

- **[30 — Survival](30_survival.html)** · all patients
  Every Kaplan–Meier and Cox model in the pipeline: treatment arm within panels defined by
  aneuploidy × MMR, then TMB, HRD, MSI, and immune content.
- **[31 — Aneuploidy vs mutation status](31_aneuploidy_mutations.html)** · MMRd only
  Aneuploidy score against each panel gene **one gene at a time** — the MMR panel and the
  Wnt genes separately — plus TP53 and the MMR union.
- **[32 — Cell-type composition vs aneuploidy](32_cell_composition.html)** · MMRd only
  Whether the mix of cells inside the annotated region differs by aneuploidy class, under
  three normalizations, with one pre-specified primary endpoint (CD45+ / all cells inside).
- **[33 — Mutation landscape](33_mutation_landscape.html)** · all patients
  Oncoplots (memo-sorted and annotation-sorted) and the TCGA Fig. 2d per-subgroup
  mutation-frequency comparison with FDR.
- **[34 — Recurrent copy number](34_recurrent_cna.html)** · all profiled
  Cohort frequency of arm-level gains and losses, and the genome-wide SCNA pileup split
  into low- and high-amplitude panels. Descriptive frequencies, no significance testing.
- **[35 — Aneuploidy × MMR copy-number contrast](35_subgroup_cna_contrast.html)** · a contrast
  Do aneuploidy-high MMRd tumours carry the same recurrent peaks as aneuploidy-high MMRp
  tumours, or reach aneuploidy by a different route?
- **[36 — Is the TMB distribution split?](36_tmb_distribution.html)** · all patients
  Whether TMB resolves the hypermutator population as a genuine second mode, under three
  independent bimodality criteria, with any high mode validated against MMR status.
- **[37 — TMB by aneuploidy and MMR](37_tmb_by_aneuploidy_and_mmr.html)** · by MMR stratum
  TMB in aneuploidy-high vs -low tumours, drawn once per MMR group so neither route to a
  high number masks the other.

### 4x — External

- **[40 — TCGA integrated classification](40_tcga_classification.html)** · all patients
  Reproduces the TCGA endometrial cascade (Kandoth et al. 2013), clustering GISTIC
  thresholded peaks with 1 − Pearson distance and Ward.D2 linkage and sweeping k = 2–8 on
  one chromosome heatmap. The serous-like call is directional; the undirected call is
  printed alongside and `[DISAGREE]` flagged when they differ.
- **[41 — TCGA UCEC replication of the TMB split](41_tcga_tmb_replication.html)** · TCGA
  The same bimodality battery on TCGA UCEC, which is tumour-normal paired and therefore
  free of the germline inflation the ancestry correction targets.

### Conventions that hold across every report

Shared explanations are written once, as child fragments in `analysis/_explainers/`, and
rendered into every report that needs them — so a reader of any single knitted page still
gets the whole explanation, and there is only one copy to keep correct.

- `tmb-two-definitions` — TMB always means one of exactly two things, and why.
- `aneuploidy-classes` — the ASCETS score and the configured high/low cut.
- `highlight-groups` — gold marks the multi-modal subset, magenta marks sample 21S188.
- `cohort-mmrd` — what "MMR-deficient only" means, and that MSI-high is a correlate.
- `master-provenance` — what `attend_master_joined` is and how it was built.

Reports show derivations and results. They carry no takeaway or interpretation sections:
conclusions belong in the manuscript, where they can be revised as the data changes.

### Configuration lives in one place

- `code/attend_harmonise.R` — ID spaces, the two crosswalks, the collapse-to-patient rule.
- `code/attend_classes.R` — column names (`attend_cols`), thresholds, class derivation,
  gene panels, the TMB definitions and labels, and the CNV/TCGA-cascade config.
- `code/attend_plots.R` — shared palettes, `attend_theme()`, the highlight overlay.
- `code/attend_ihc.R` — FlowPath IHC metric definitions (reports 20, 30, 32).
- `code/attend_scna.R` — GISTIC peak union, panel score, permutation and LOO stability
  (report 35).
- `code/attend_bimodality.R` — the bimodality measures shared by reports 36 and 41.
